newsitem.title: RUSSIA: New Russian budget draft will not pass Duma-deputy.
newsitem.headline: New Russian budget draft will not pass Duma-deputy.

text.p: The Russian 1997 draft budget agreed to in a reconciliation commission will probably be rejected by the State Duma lower house next week, dooming its chances of passing this year, a senior deputy said on Thursday.
"In this shape, there is not much chance," Alexei Golovkov, deputy chairman of the lower house of parliament Duma budget committee.

Golovkov told reporters that deputies were divided over the size of the projected federal budget deficit, which was set at 95.4 trillion roubles or 3.5 percent of gross domestic product in the draft approved by a thin margin on Wednesday.
Members of both houses of parliament and the government are on the committee.

If the budget is rejected by the Duma, the government will be required to rework it within 20 days, and rejection next week would practically ensure that parliament would not be able to vote it through four required readings by year end.
Golovkov said parliament would be forced to pass monthly or quarterly budgets which would cause confusion throughout the economy.

Economic-reform minded deputies want a lower budget deficit to achieve lower credit rates, which they say are vital for economic growth and but which are kept high through heavy government borrowing, but the Communists want to increase spending.
The entire Duma, in which Communists and their sympathisers are the largest bloc, is likely to give the new budget draft a first reading on November 20 or 22.
